alex: Repro for a leak in the Go sampleapp when auth refresh happens midstream. CPU climbs, goroutines pile up.

alex: TL;DR: token rotates while generator.Pull is active; app re-inits client and retries, but old Pull goroutine never exits.

alex: Minimal pattern we used:
```go
for {
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parent, 30*time.Second)
  go func() {
    for m := range client.Pull(ctx) { handle(m) }
  }()
  // refresh can happen here -> create new client and retry
  cancel()
}
```

sara: sdk version? do you reuse client or recreate?

alex: v0.9.1, we recreate client after refresh to pick up creds.

cheng: sounds like the goroutine is stuck in stream.Next()/Recv blocked on network; cancel didn't propagate because the stream handshake isn't closed when client is replaced.

kevin: we've hit this when transient 401 triggers reinit. The old persistConn can block in readLoop and Next never returns.

alex: stack snippet:
```
runtime.goexit
github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/gen.(*stream).Next
net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop
```

alex: quick local workaround: call stream.Close() and wait for goroutine to exit before recreating client. fixes leak.

sara: patch suggestion for sampleapp: avoid spawning goroutines that capture child ctx; handle stream inline and defer Close(); select on ctx.Done().

cheng: SDK followups: add a helper that ensures stream closed on exit (WithStream(ctx, fn)) and doc the auth-refresh pattern. Also make Next() check parent ctx cancel more aggressively.

kevin: filed issue #1423 to add helper + docs; assigned to eng-ml. Immediate step: update sampleapp with explicit Close() and avoid fire-and-forget goroutines. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: created branch fix/onboard-stream-close-1758009999

alex: I'll open a PR with the sampleapp fix + short runbook steps for reproducer.
